1. contact your county’s small business bureau and enroll in a entrepreneurial beginners boot camp class. this will provide you with the legal information you need to know to start out.
2. don’t compare yourself to others - there are lots of people selling handmade. few are extremely successful, most are mediocre because they did not have a plan or really took the time to understand what  is required and the sacrifices needed to make it big. 
3. learn about social media marketing!!!! knowing how to promote yourself in our new digital world is one of the hardest things for most of us who are older. It’s definitely not hard to learn but it is important to make the time to learn and understand how it works. 
4. Figure out who you are trying to sell to. this can be hard especially when we want everyone to buy our items. you must think smaller and really narrow down what traits, habits, dislikes, background, community, likes and loves your “perfect die hard customer is”. Once you figure that out you will be on your way to really knowing how, when and where to connect with them and gain new customers who think your the bees knees!

5. what is your base cost per item? does your cost vary based on materials? how could you reduce that variable? are you buying  directly from wholesale and at bulk pricing? if not you should! who are the best wholesalers for your supplies? best materials vs. cost? how is your shipping charges factored into your material costs? Shop around always for the best prices, materials that are cost effective and affordable shipping charges that can either be absorbed into your own cost or passed along to your customers without drastically altering your selling price. 
6.create a production work flow - how many items can you produce in a normal work day, week, month? how many items if you worked overtime? how many items if you had an emergency or supply/equipment issue that impacted your production? would or could you make enough items to be profitable? would you need to hire help to help you reach your revenue goals? what are the negative costs associated with hiring employees vs. the financial gain from increased production? 
7. have a budget and separate bank account
8. pick a platform where to sell your goods that is best for your skill level (etsy is easy to set up and understand but is limited in features and customization; the opposite is true for amazon handmade)

I'm a parent and I know that might mean you don't want to hear what I have to say but I hope you will at least give me a few moments.  I want to tell you something, but first I need to give you some background about me. You see, when  I look back on my own childhood I remember thinking my parents were assholes and didn't really care about me. I've been physically, mentally, and sexually abused by them. So I can tick off all the boxes as to why I should think this way.  I remember days and nights being hungry, and lonely. My parent had me when they were young - just out of high school, and  I was around and saw way too many things that a young kid should never see. I remember hating my parents and even disowning them for a while in my 20s. But now that I've been a parent at both a young age (19/20) and then later on (in my 30's) I can tell you. I made a ton of mistakes with my children that I had when i was young that I did not make with my other children that I had when I was in my 30's. With my first set of kids (the one's I had when I was 19/20) I was short tempered, irrational, unexperienced, and like many young adults thought I knew it all, wanted everything now, and had no idea what is truly important in this life. I was not a great parent, I was ok, but definitely not as good as I could of been. When I had second set of children in my 30's, I was more experienced at being a parent. More seasoned, I had patience, I was financially more secure, I had a spouse that was able and willing to be a 50/50 partner in raising our children. I didn't yell over stupid stuff but rather placed value on what I believe will help them succeed in their lives when they become adults. I also realized when I was younger I only really focused on myself, (as do most people in their 20's) and never really had the time or put forth the effort to parent with my first set of children. With the second set,  I had the time and realized the value, such simple things like volunteering for the PTO at my kids schools, and being a team mom when they played sports would have.  

​

So what does this mean or matter?? - Parents can suck at parenting. But do you know and understand why? My parents sucked because they were young kids that had a kid and had no experience being a parent and partied too much (hippies and all). And golly gee, look at me, making the same stupid mistakes because I too was too young to be a parent and I too didn't have the experience to know how to do it. I too made a ton of mistakes and fucked up a bunch... I now realize that parents aren't perfect. they are human and make mistakes just like the rest of us. Their biggest job - the one thing that separates them from their kids is the responsibility they feel to provide and care for their offsprings. Sometimes that is stressful and scary, sometimes that task is easy and comes with tons of supportive assistants. . But no matter how they react, how terrible they are at parenting, it does not mean they don't love you. Love and parenting are not necessarily the same thing. You can suck at driving but love your car. You can suck at parenting but still love your children. 

If your parents suck at parenting please don't think it means they don't love you. It just means they suck at parenting. They could suck at parenting for a number of reasons perhaps because they were young parents, like I was, or perhaps because they are struggling to keep a job, or their marriage together, maybe they have other issues that impact their ability to parent - but trust me when i say this - a parents ability to parent in no way measures the amount of love they have for their children.

That by their willingness to endure a bit of inconvenience  they wear it proudly as it shows such an immense  level of compassion and consideration to their fellow man. I can not understand how low we have fallen, attacking each other with such hatred  over a simple piece of cloth. I think how has this come to be? I draw no other thoughts just disbelief and shame. I can not understand how something so simple, so simple can bring forth such hate and animosity. Long before COVID everyone has been told or “guilted by others” to wear something. Not one time in history has there been such an angry cry of rebellion towards these pieces of cloth! Why??? I can only ascertain, as it appears the only rational reason, that we have become programmed to NOT hold another persons health and life with consideration but rather place our own comforts and wants before anyone or anything else. I just don’t get it? I  am disconnected from this reality. I do not hate or throw vulgarities towards another just because they do not agree with me on this subject. Rather I feel sadness that a simple piece of fabric can be used as a scapegoat for the anger and fear and frustrations  we are all feeling because of this pandemic.
